evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; 形義通解
evidence.text: The database interprets 面’s oracle forms as a facial outline with an eye and identifies ‘face’ as the original sense. It reports that 面 itself is not attested in bronze inscriptions, though a related bronze graph uses 𦣻 with an enclosure. It also reports a Chu-slip enclosure altered toward 臼 and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are the database’s analyses and reported examples; no individual artifact was inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 麵 is written 麪 in Shuowen, analyzed as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic, and glossed ‘wheat powder’ (麥末也; Duan’s text has 麥屑末也). It describes 麵 as a later common writing and reports equivalence in 玉篇 and 廣韻. It cites flour or food examples in 後漢書, 南史, and Tang poetry; those citations do not establish first-use dates for flour and noodle senses.
evidence.title: A04763 麵 — 教育部《異體字字典》

No 麵 row is supplied in that local table, so these data do not establish a same-system sound comparison between 面 and 麵. The notation is Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction, not a pronunciation of an ancient depicted object.

search_audit.query: 面 oracle bone form face 甲骨 CUHK character paleography; site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/dictView.jsp 麵 麪 麥 丏 面; 面 麵 pronunciation Baxter Sagart Old Chinese 麪 phonetic 丏
search_audit.outcome: Fresh search located the CUHK paleographic page, both Taiwan Ministry entries, CUHK 麵 entry, secondary Baxter–Sagart transcription, and official Baxter–Sagart PDF. Inspected the CUHK and Ministry pages and Wiktionary. PDF and both official Unihan pages returned internal errors. Local supplied B–S and Unihan rows were treated only as local cross-checks.

gaps: No individual oracle inscription was inspected or dated; the face interpretation is CUHK’s analysis. The source reports 面 itself absent from bronze inscriptions but does not specify corpus coverage.

The Chu-slip form change toward 臼 and ‘face toward’ use are reported by CUHK; the artifact and text were not independently inspected. Dates and semantic links for surface, side, and dimension remain unresolved.

麪’s 麥-plus-丏 analysis and 麵 as a later spelling are supported, but available inspected sources do not establish the exact transition chronology or separate earliest written attestations for flour and noodle senses.

麵’s source-word pronunciation and its relationship to 面 cannot be independently compared in Baxter–Sagart from the available local rows: 面 has *C.me[n]-s / mjienH, while 麵 is absent. Do not infer a whole-graph loan from matching modern miàn; the documented account identifies 丏 as 麪’s phonetic component and 面 as the later 麵 phonetic spelling.

Official Unihan pages for U+9762 and U+9EB5 returned internal errors, so the requested click-through confirmation of current kMandarin readings could not be obtained. The local rows give miàn for both.
The official Baxter–Sagart PDF failed to open; the exact local 面 row and the secondary transcription agree, but no 麵 row supports a same-system comparison.
